item.title: Belize Reef Restoration Effort: Lisa Carne revives storm-hit corals; project outplants 100,000 fragments
item.description: In 2001, Hurricane Iris wreaked havoc on Belize's coral reefs, sparking an innovative restoration effort. Marine biologist Lisa Carne took the lead in replanting coral fragments, which were often neglected. Through her organization, Fragments of Hope, more than 100,000 corals have been successfully restored, resulting in a remarkable boost in coral coverage and marine biodiversity.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Dating to 1898, Nipomo's oldest church donated after 128 years to become a community hub
item.description: A historic church in Nipomo, California, dating to 1898, has been donated to the Dana Adobe and Cultural Center by its owners, John and Rebecca Prewett. The building will be developed into a museum, event venue and “Visit Nipomo” centre, while Calvary Church will continue holding Sunday services there.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Las Vegas developers buy 940 acres of former federal desert for $94 million; 6,000-home community planned
item.description: A large federal desert parcel near Las Vegas will become Monument Hills, a new master-planned community. This development will feature up to 6,000 homes and various amenities for residents. The $94 million land deal is the largest BLM transaction in the valley for decades. Proceeds from the sale will fund projects across Nevada, including parks and education. First homes are anticipated to be available around spring 2028.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Actor Max Thieriot bought a 90-acre ranch in 2013; his Sonoma Hollywood retreat is now a vineyard
item.description: Max Thieriot’s roughly 90-acre Sonoma County ranch has evolved since he and his wife Lexi bought it in 2013. The property now includes the nine-acre Bodega Thieriot Pinot noir vineyard, while the rest remains hillside, woodland and pasture. Though the actor’s family now lives in Washington state for most of the year, he continues returning to the ranch during the off-season.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Snake grows a fake spider on its tail to lure birds; scans reveal surprisingly normal bones inside
item.description: Researchers utilized XCT scanning technology to investigate the unique tail of a viper. The imaging uncovered the presence of standard viper vertebrae within the tail's unusual form. This finding underscores the discrepancies that can exist between external appearance and internal skeletal makeup. Fossilized remains alone may not capture the true look of an organism, while museum specimens remain crucial for advancing our understanding through innovative methods.

item.title: Steven Spielberg bought an LA horse ranch for $5.75M; 27 years later, he is selling it for $29.9M
item.description: Steven Spielberg and his wife are selling their stunning Los Angeles ranch for $29.9 million, a significant increase from the $5.75 million they invested in 1999. This gorgeous property features premium equestrian facilities and lavish living quarters. Earlier dreams of a five-story riding stable were scrapped, but the ranch has been a vital component of their real estate holdings for almost three decades.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: South China Sea methane leak formed a 1km plume; worms and bacteria built a ‘worm bed’ in 2 years
item.description: A South China Sea drilling incident caused a significant methane leak in 2018. Ocean scientists observed an ecosystem rapidly responding to the underwater gas release. Bacteria and worms quickly formed a methane-munching 'worm bed' within two years. This new biofilter degraded methane effectively, reducing plume height significantly. However, this rapid ecosystem development caused a notable decrease in original microbial diversity.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Man lost his ring in 1973; 53 years later, fate brings it back
item.description: In 1973, a Kansas student misplaced his class ring during an epic snowball fight. Fast forward fifty-three years later, campus workers discovered the ring while tending to the grounds. Interestingly, the owner and his wife were driving through the city that same day, having just discussed the ring a week earlier. Now, the couple will restore and treasure the sentimental piece.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: $250M crypto fraud allegedly funded six homes, Lamborghinis and dozens of Louis Vuitton bags
item.description: Christopher Alexander Delgado admitted to a $250 million crypto fraud scheme. His company, Goliath Ventures, promised investor returns from liquidity pools. Instead, funds paid earlier investors and funded a lavish personal lifestyle. Delgado purchased numerous luxury properties, vehicles, and designer accessories. He now faces significant prison time and asset forfeiture for his actions.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Miami flight overrun: Plane touched down at nearly 300 kmph despite high-speed warning
item.description: A 21 Air Boeing 767 touched down at Miami International Airport at an alarming speed of nearly 300 kmph. As the crew attempted to execute a go-around following the landing, they had neglected to deploy the speed brakes, leading to automated alerts about the steep descent and proximity to the ground. Investigators are now analyzing the flight data and cockpit voice recordings to uncover further insights regarding this incident.
item.dc:creator: Vijaya Srivastava

item.title: 1,700 passengers boarded an Alaska cruise, only for Royal Caribbean to cancel it two days later
item.description: Royal Caribbean cancelled an Alaska cruise after around 1,700 passengers had already boarded the ship in Vancouver. The seven-night sailing was delayed because of an unspecified technical issue and was later cancelled after passengers spent two days waiting on board. Guests were offered refunds, future cruise credit and help with travel changes.

item.title: After Trump renamed Lake Ontario, Pennsylvania Republican seeks ‘Lake Pennsylvania’ for Erie
item.description: US President Donald Trump has signed an executive order directing federal agencies to rename Lake Ontario as “Lake America” on US maps, documents and databases. Canada has rejected the move, while several US governors have also said they will continue calling it Lake Ontario. The decision comes amid rising trade tensions between Washington and Ottawa.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 1982, Israel released 28 wild donkeys; 44 years later, they created a desert oasis
item.description: In an effort to rejuvenate the parched landscape of Israel's Ramon Crater, wild donkeys were brought back into the ecosystem. These resilient animals played a crucial role by creating waterholes, which became essential for desert wildlife. Additionally, their droppings helped spread acacia seeds, promoting the growth of trees. Their natural movements resulted in water-retaining depressions, significantly transforming the area's ecology into a thriving environment that has caught global attention.

item.title: Dam Removal Restores Creek: Buckhorn Creek flows freely again; volunteers plant trees
item.description: After more than a century, the Buckhorn Creek dam has been dismantled, reviving its original flow for the first time in 125 years. A modern ninety-foot bridge now crosses the creek, enhancing access for trail enthusiasts. This ecological restoration significantly improves aquatic habitats, particularly supporting brook trout populations. Additionally, volunteers will introduce native plants along the banks to help stabilize the soil.
